reasoning: The proposal is essentially a reproduction of experiments the source paper itself already ran. Tice et al. (arXiv 2412.01784, NeurIPS 2025) explicitly tested 7-8B open models — Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Phi-3-small, and password-locked Mistral-7B — using the exact proposed method (Gaussian weight-noise sweep over σ∈[0,0.01], an "improvement ratio" metric of peak-vs-baseline accuracy, N=5 seeds) on the exact proposed benchmarks (MMLU, AI2/ARC, WMDP), under both prompted and fine-tuned sandbagging, reporting improvement-ratio success rates of 61% (Llama-8B) to 100% (Mistral-7B) and a threshold classifier with AUC~1.0 in several settings. The proposal's secondary question of whether separation is "sharp enough to threshold reliably" is also already addressed: both the paper and follow-up community work ("Fuzzing LLMs sometimes makes them reveal their secrets", LessWrong) report the signal is real but unreliable/variable on smaller models. The only novelty is a minor model-version bump (Llama-3.1 vs 3.0; adding Qwen2.5-7B, already noted as noise-resilient elsewhere), which does not change the answered status of the underlying question.

evidence.title: Noise Injection Reveals Hidden Capabilities of Sandbagging Language Models (Tice et al.)
evidence.summary: The source paper itself. Tests the proposed method on small open models including Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Phi-3-small, and password-locked Mistral-7B on MMLU/AI2/WMDP. Uses Gaussian noise σ∈[0,0.01], improvement-ratio metric, N=5 trials, and a threshold classifier reaching AUC~1.0 in several settings; reports per-model improvement-ratio success rates (Llama-8B 61%, Mistral-7B-finetuned 100%). This directly covers the proposal's reproduction-on-7-8B-models question and the threshold-reliability question.

evidence.title: Noise Injection Increases the Accuracy of Sandbagging LLMs
evidence.summary: Workshop version of the same work confirming the noise-injection accuracy-recovery effect on sandbagging models, including small open models, with the improvement-ratio detector.

evidence.title: Fuzzing LLMs sometimes makes them reveal their secrets
evidence.summary: Community follow-up directly addressing the proposal's 'sharp enough to threshold reliably' question: weight-noise (fuzzing) uplift on sandbagging models is real but unreliable, and weaker on fine-tuned sandbaggers than prompted ones — meaning the reliability/separation question is already empirically characterized.

evidence.title: Adding noise to a sandbagging model can reveal its true capabilities
evidence.summary: Author summary of the Tice et al. method confirming the prompted-sandbagging vs honest separation on small open instruct models, the same experimental setup the proposal would re-run.
